claim: The Formant agent is a program installed on a Linux target that uploads telemetry to the Formant cloud, acts as a WebRTC teleoperation peer, executes commands defined in Formant, and applies device configuration (streams, rates, agent updates) pushed from the web app
Formant agent supported configurations (agent page): Ubuntu 24.04/ROS 2 Jazzy, 22.04/ROS 2 Humble, 20.04/ROS 1 Noetic, 18.04/ROS 1 Melodic, each on amd64 and arm64

[Docs inconsistent] Formant's System requirements page lists a different agent OS set (Ubuntu 22.04/20.04/18.04 and Debian 9/10/11, amd64/arm64), so the two official pages disagree on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian support

Formant docs: the native Debian/Ubuntu install via convenience script 'is not officially supported'; Docker installation is 'highly recommended'; the install command carries a provisioning token that expires after 72 hours and needs sudo apt
The Formant agent is distributed as an apt package from a Formant repository whose key is fetched with apt-key; it is updated in place with 'sudo apt upgrade formant-agent' (no OS image, no A/B)

Formant telemetry uploads at 0.5 Hz by default; the agent can buffer data on the device and upload only on demand, so a steady internet link is not required after install (internet is required to install)
Formant teleoperation is WebRTC peer-to-peer; Twilio sets up the connection and relays traffic over TURN on restrictive networks; *.twilio.com and *.formant.io must be reachable
Formant's web terminal runs as the non-root 'formant' user and fctl offers port forwarding; both can be disabled on the robot with FORMANT_DISABLE_TERMINAL=true / FORMANT_PORT_FORWARDING=false

Formant Terms of Service (last updated 2026-04-16) define the Agent, the Formant Platform and 'Formant AI' as Formant Technology owned by Formant, and offer 'Customer-Hosted Software' (private cloud or VPC deployment) as a licensed option
GitHub FormantIO/formant (Apache-2.0, commit 64bcdb0, 2026-10-29) holds 'software releases and other resources for development with Formant' (SDK, protos, examples), not the agent source

[SECONDARY: press-release reprint] Formant launched F3 on 2025-06-30: a generative-AI interface to the whole platform, a 24/7 'agentic' monitoring layer and agents for multi-step investigations, built on third-party models (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini)

[SECONDARY] Formant raised USD 21M led by BMW i Ventures (2023-10-11); the CEO said the platform powers 'tens of thousands of production robots'; Formant launched Theopolis, an AI language interface, in 2023

[Vendor marketing] Formant's 2026 homepage positions it as 'the operating layer for physical AI', claims 644 production organizations (platform telemetry, May 2026), and sells via a discovery session; formant.io/pricing returns 404, so no public price list
The Formant web application supports Google Chrome only
Formant docs index lists Google SSO and OIDC SSO, bulk and automated agent provisioning, device configuration templates, device groups and an Agent SDK

Foxglove's device-side software has three parts: the open-source SDK (C++, Python, Rust; logs MCAP and streams live), the Foxglove Bridge (a ROS 1/ROS 2 package wrapping the SDK) and Foxlet (a daemon that watches a directory for recordings and imports them; not a live data source)
Foxlet (formerly 'Foxglove Agent') ships for amd64 and arm64 as a .deb, a static binary and a Docker image

Foxglove remote access: a WebRTC gateway on the device authenticates with a device token and connects out; Foxglove provides STUN/TURN and an SFU; images become adaptive-bitrate video and point clouds are Draco-compressed by default

Foxglove Edge Sites (up to 1,000 per organization) keep recordings on premises until imported; the edge controller installs as a Debian package, static binary, Docker image or Helm chart on Kubernetes
An on-premises Foxglove Primary Site needs Kubernetes 1.30+, Helm 3.12+ and an S3-compatible object store (tested with MinIO)
Foxglove pricing: Free USD 0 (10 GB, 3 users, 5 devices); Pro USD 20/month + usage (1 TB, billed by monthly active devices); Enterprise custom, with self-hosted data and on-premises deployment

Foxglove shipped the last open-source Foxglove Studio (v1.87.0) in February 2024 and has since shipped 50+ commercial releases; the foxglove/studio repo is archived with no licence metadata (GitHub API)
foxglove-sdk is MIT (release sdk/v0.30.3, 2026-10-26) and now contains the ROS 2 foxglove_bridge package, also MIT

Foxglove agents: an in-app agent sidebar that asks approval before changing anything, a Slack integration, and a desktop-only local MCP server on 127.0.0.1:7333 with a bearer token (Pro/Enterprise/Academic plan and a developer seat)

Foxglove's MCP server adds no approval step of its own: it runs any tool the client calls, marks tools read-only or destructive via MCP annotations, and attributes actions to the signed-in user rather than the agent; agents can list devices read-only
Foxglove desktop has a standalone licence mode for offline and air-gapped machines (.req/.lic file exchange); cloud features are unavailable in it
viam-server is built from the RDK, which is licensed AGPL-3.0
viam-agent is AGPL-3.0 (latest release v1.2.1, 2026-11-02, per the releases API); the Python SDK is Apache-2.0 (GitHub licence API)
The micro-RDK (viam-micro-server) targets the ESP32 and is AGPL-3.0 (GitHub licence API)

viam-agent is a systemd service that manages viam-server, first-boot Wi-Fi hotspot or Bluetooth provisioning, OS settings (package updates, log forwarding) and networking, polling the cloud at least every 5 s

viam-agent updates viam-server and itself by downloading to a cache, checking SHA-256 and swapping an atomic symlink (old binary kept 30 days); it does not roll back automatically and keeps retrying a crashing version until the cloud config pins an older one
Code agrees with docs: the Versions struct tracks a PreviousVersion 'for (TODO) rollback'; a SHA-256 mismatch aborts the install; the new binary is symlinked into bin and takes effect after restart

viam-agent OS updates are in-place package upgrades: 'all'/'security' delegate to unattended-upgrades on Debian/Raspberry Pi OS (Bullseye, Bookworm, Trixie); 'managed-*' modes run dnf, apt-get or yum (and Windows Update) themselves and hold reboots for the maintenance window; there is no A/B image
viam-agent reports ext4 error counters as a storage-health signal because SD cards have no SMART data

viam-server caches its config locally and can run on it for up to 60 days offline; when online it checks for new config every 15 s and reconfigures resources live; earlier configs can be restored from History

Viam rollouts: modules track latest by default, or pin to a version or fragment tag; maintenance windows need a boolean sensor (no time-based schedule); there is no canary or percentage rollout, and the fleet dashboard does not show per-machine versions
viam-agent is installed with a machine-specific 'curl ... install.sh | sh' one-liner that embeds the machine API key; a preinstall script exists for baking it into device images

Viam runs a remote, OAuth-authenticated MCP server scoped to the user's existing permissions; its 'Live machine (destructive)' tools (e.g. call_machine_api, run_docommand) can move hardware and 'act immediately, with no draft and no undo'; live tools use the machine's default API key and create one if missing
Viam API keys are scoped to a machine, location or organization and by default have full write access to that scope; per-resource, per-method limits are optional via user_permissions
Viam's in-app AI assistant turns plain-language requests into staged config changes that apply only on Save; diagnostic shell commands it proposes each need explicit approval

Viam pricing: first USD 5/month of cloud usage free, then usage-based (e.g. tabular data USD 0.25/GB-month, non-tabular USD 0.05/GB-month, upload USD 0.15/GB, egress USD 0.25/GB, compute USD 0.0025/s); no per-device fee is listed
Every Viam resource has a typed API (e.g. rdk:component:arm), a model and a name; APIs are protobuf over gRPC and a machine can list its resources and methods at runtime
Viam's setup wizard can run a machine as a cloud simulation before hardware exists; simulation is billed per minute
Viam docs carry setup guides for Raspberry Pi, Jetson AGX Orin and Jetson Nano/Orin Nano; viam-agent OS modes cover Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS, Fedora, RHEL-family and Windows
balena markets balenaCloud and balenaOS for robots, drones and autonomous vehicles (containers, OTA, device management) and links ROS 'robot block' and multi-drone simulation posts
balena's ROS 2 example (balena-io-examples/balena-ros2-foxy-desktop) is archived, last pushed 2023-06-17, and targets ROS 2 Foxy, which reached end of life on 2023-06-20
[SECONDARY: user forum, 2019-10] A team porting a ROS application from Ubuntu 16.04 to balena on Jetson TX2 bought balena's custom-device support and praised it

[SECONDARY: ROS Discourse, 2023-10] Teams with 10+ ROS 2 robots compared dual-copy (A/B) and container updates: one leaned to Mender; one 'settled on Balena' because it does both (Yocto A/B for the OS, Docker for apps) and was told its pricing is 'quite steep'; another uses RAUC Yocto images plus Podman with rootless, unprivileged containers per ROS 2 node
